name: Nagraj
summary: Raj Comics' snake king: a hero with deadly venom and millions of microscopic snakes living in his body. He debuted in 1986 as the publisher's first superhero.
origin: Nagraj was born to King Takshakraj and Queen Lalita of the kingdom of Takshaknagar. Because of a plot by his uncle Nagpasha, he was born blue and lifeless and, following custom, set adrift on a river. Guided by the snake deity Deva Kaljayi, the shapeshifting snake rulers of the hidden island Nagdweep began to heal him. The evil scientist Professor Nagmani later raised the boy and sent him out as a mind-controlled terror weapon. On his first mission Nagraj was defeated by the 300-year-old sage Baba Gorakhnath, who removed the control capsule from his head. Nagraj became his disciple and swore to fight crime and terror.
powers: Lethal venom through touch, bite and poisonous breath
Millions of microscopic snakes in his body, used as ropes, shields and spies
Can break into particles to turn briefly invisible and intangible
Can fuse with allies into combined forms
Telepathic contact and communication with snakes

storyline.title: Professor Nagmani's weapon
storyline.beat: Nagraj's first mission is to steal a golden statue of a Goddess from a temple. He pulls it off, but then Baba Gorakhnath beats him, frees his mind, and turns the weapon into a hero.

storyline.title: War on world terror
storyline.beat: The original run tours the world fighting terrorists and gangsters across 44 issues drawn by a rotating team of artists, ending with Visarpi Ki Shadi in 1995.

storyline.title: Meeting Dhruva
storyline.beat: Special #1, Nagraj aur Super Commando Dhruv, is Raj Comics' first multi-hero special and pairs its two biggest stars.

storyline.title: The mythic Nagraj
storyline.beat: Anupam Sinha takes over writing and art, telling multi-part epics like the Khazana arc, challenging snake-gods, and making the Two-in-One comics that combine Nagraj and Dhruva roughly yearly.

storyline.title: Many Nagrajs
storyline.beat: Raj Comics splits the hero into parallel series, including the terror-fighting Aatankharta Nagraj (from Hari Maut, 2007) and the horror-flavoured Narak Nashak Nagraj.

gossip.text: Manoj Gupta came up with a snake-themed hero in 1985 because snakes carry deep religious and mythological meaning in India.
Nagraj started out as a villain's weapon. His very first mission was a temple robbery.
A 1997 TV advert for Nagraj starred a young Sonu Sood.
In 2019 it was reported that Ranveer Singh could play Nagraj in a Karan Johar production, and Raj Comics president Manoj Gupta welcomed the idea. The film has not been made.
The character draws on legends of shapeshifting ichchhadhari snakes and the vishmanushya, a mythical venomous human.

quiz.q: Who freed Nagraj from Professor Nagmani's mind control?
quiz.why: The ancient sage Baba Gorakhnath removed the capsule implanted in Nagraj's head.
He carries millions of tiny snakes that he can send out as tools and weapons.

quiz.q: Which of these is one of Nagraj's main weaknesses?
quiz.why: Severe cold makes him drowsy and pushes him toward hibernation, which is why the ice snake Sheetnag Kumar guards him.

theme.tagline: Hug him at your own risk. He is extremely venomous.

timeline.title: Raj Comics' first superhero
timeline.note: GENL #14 brings in a venom-blooded hero who starts out as a mad scientist's weapon before switching sides.

timeline.title: First team-up with Dhruva
timeline.note: Special #1 puts the snake king and Super Commando Dhruva on one cover. It is also Raj Comics' first multi-hero special.

timeline.title: Anupam Sinha takes over
timeline.note: Sinha steps in as writer and artist and steers Nagraj toward longer, myth-soaked epics.

timeline.title: Hari Maut opens a new front
timeline.note: Hari Maut launches a world-terrorism line of stories, giving the hero a harder, globe-trotting edge.

timeline.title: Nagayana wraps up
timeline.note: Iti Kaand closes Nagayana, an eight-part futuristic saga built around Nagraj and Dhruva.

timeline.title: First animated film
timeline.note: The first of five animated films, the My Name is Raj series, comes out; the last arrives in 2021.

timeline.title: Live-action buzz
timeline.note: Ranveer Singh is reported as a possible Nagraj in a film produced by Karan Johar.

timeline.title: One hero, three publishers
timeline.note: In October 2020 Raj Comics splits into three separate entities, led by Sanjay, Manoj and Manish Gupta.

facts.text: Sanjay Gupta says the Spider-Man cartoon he saw on Indian TV in the early 1980s inspired Nagraj. Scholar Suchitra Mathur spots the echo in his animal motif, science-lab roots and snake-rope swinging.
In 1997 Raj Comics won plagiarism cases against Radha Comics' Nagesh and Goel Comics' Nagputra, two close copies of Nagraj. Sahapedia calls them among India's first comic-book lawsuits.
Demand was so intense that a new Nagraj issue was needed every two weeks, Manoj Gupta recalled, so he and his brother Sanjay shut themselves in a room every Sunday and came out with a fresh script.
In the comics, Nagraj's venom traces back through Deva Kaljayi to Shiva's venom from the churning of the ocean, a link between a pulp hero and Hindu mythology.
Cold is one of Nagraj's main weaknesses and can push him toward hibernation, while his icy snake-friend Sheetnag Kumar lives in his body and shields him from freezing.
Nagraj can fuse with allies. With an ally named Lava he became Agni-Nagraj, a form that breathed venomous flame and released burning snakes.
Nagayana, an eight-part saga, retells the Ramayana with Raj Comics heroes in the roles. It started as a planned four-part series and grew to eight, ending with a 128-page finale on 10 March 2009.
Nagraj Strikes: The Attack of the Coronaman, a 2020 comic, was made in about 72 hours, the fastest Raj Comics ever produced, and was conceived on day four of India's lockdown.
Mongooses haunt Nagraj's tale. His uncle Nagpasha tricked the queen into offering a dead mongoose to the Snake God, and Baba Gorakhnath keeps a mystic black mongoose named Shikangi.
Nagraj was born with blue skin, and after treatment on the hidden snake island of Nagdweep his colour turned green. Greenman and Green Death are among his listed aliases.
Nagraj can split his body into particles and rejoin them in about three seconds, which makes him briefly invisible and untouchable.

Nagraj's enemies come from around the world: an ancient Egyptian mummy whose power comes from his mask, a scientist from Japan called Miss Killer, and Thodanga, a creature that is part human, part turtle and part rhinoceros.
In the late 1990s Raj Comics shot a few episodes of a live-action Nagraj TV show that never aired. Three episodes were given away on CDs with digest-sized comics.
Nagraj's breath, called vish-funkar, blows his venom out as vapour, and depending on strength it can cause blindness, drowsiness or blackouts, and once even started a fire.
Naagu is the most cheerful and comical of the snakes living inside Nagraj. It is hard to tell whether he is a jester or a helper, and he loves watching movies.
Visarpi is the queen of Nagdweep and Nagraj's love interest. The original 44-issue run ended in 1995 with the issue Visarpi Ki Shadi, meaning Visarpi's wedding.
Bharti is Nagraj's friend and business partner. She secretly fights crime under the name Faceless, and she is one-sidedly in love with him.
Nagraj's arch-enemy is his own immortal, venomous uncle Nagpasha, who caused his parents' deaths. Nagpasha's guru is the mechanically brilliant scientist Gurudev, who wants to rule the world.
Nagdant is a jealous, weaker copy of Nagraj, built by Professor Nagmani, the same scientist who first raised the hero.
Kentuki, a student of the villain Gurudev, is a physically powerful snake with the strength of fifty elephants, one of the toughest muscle-men in Nagraj's long list of enemies.
Saudaangi is a snake-woman from an Egyptian clan who lives in Nagraj's body. She has thorns in her snake form and some tantra knowledge, and her clan fights the mummy of pharaoh Tutankhamun.
Five animated Nagraj films, the My Name is Raj series, were released in 2011, 2012, 2013, 2017 and 2021. Three aired on Cartoon Network India in 2015, and the last two followed in 2019 and 2021.

kidSummary: Nagraj is Raj Comics' snake king. Venom flows through him and millions of tiny snakes live in his body. He began as a scientist's weapon, then a sage named Baba Gorakhnath freed him and he turned hero.
